name: Ethics and Responsible Automation — Entry Point

stations.why: The shared opener: a vendor, a contract and a decision that must not be made by the person who benefits.
Every speaker heard before a robot's rollout is approved, with the minutes that show it.
When a robot stops in front of the public: confirm first, then speak, and say what is not yet known.
The people who live beside the site are asked before it changes, not after.
Owning a harm the automation caused, without deflecting it.
A supervisor's feedback on a near-miss, named to the behaviour rather than the person.
The site-wide stop, drilled so the people in the aisle know what the robots will do when it is pressed.

summary: The entry point for deciding what a robot on a site is allowed to do, who answers for it, and what is said to the public when something goes wrong. Its stations are the governance and communication ones; the robot-control stations sit in the control entry point, so the two packs teach the same stop rule from two sides.
union: AFSCME and SEIU public-service staff, and the site supervisors who answer for an automated site; taught as a civic course, not a union apprenticeship
